title: oncall: quick diagnostics CLI and playbook templates catalog
author: Aisha Thompson
release_notes: Add a lightweight on-call diagnostics CLI for grabbing ephemeral traces and system snapshots; introduce a catalog of YAML playbook templates for common incident classes; add docs and quickstart guide for on-call responders; no breaking API changes.
body: Title: oncall: quick diagnostics CLI and playbook templates catalog. Summary: Introduces a tiny, dependency-light CLI (slo-quickdiag) for on-call responders to capture short-lived diagnostics (process list, top-N spans, recent logs, ephemeral trace sampler) and upload a timeboxed evidence bundle to the incident storage bucket, plus a curated catalog of YAML playbook templates to jumpstart triage for frequent incident classes (latency spike, OOM, KV cache missstorm, autoscaler thrash). Motivation: During several Pager rotations we observed responders spending 5–15 minutes collecting the same set of artifacts before they can start triage. This PR reduces mean time-to-evidence and standardizes the first-responder checklist so playbooks and automated evaluators can consume consistent snapshot shapes. Design: The CLI is intentionally minimal: a single Python entrypoint (click-based) that shells out to existing local tools when present (strace, perf) but falls back to internal samplers. Evidence bundles are JSON+tar.gz with strict size and TTL metadata; the default sample window is 30s with an optional --long 3m flag. Playbook templates are parameterized YAML and registered in a small registry file for discovery by the console and incident-bot. Backwards compatibility: No server API changes. All behavior is opt-in; upload requires an oncall role token. Checklist: - [x] implement CLI core sampling and local collection - [x] implement uploader and signed-URL flow - [x] implement playbook YAML catalog and registry - [x] add unit and integration tests for sampler - [x] add quickstart docs and examples - [x] run security review of bundle contents Commits summary: 1) Implement quickdiag CLI and basic samplers; 2) Add uploader and evidence bundle schema; 3) Add playbook templates and registry; 4) Docs: quickstart and oncall runbook; 5) Tests and CI fixes; 6) Address review feedback (permission checks, smaller bundles). Files changed (high level): - src/cli/quickdiag.py: new CLI entrypoint with sampling commands and uploader integration (approx 420 lines). - src/cli/samplers/process_snapshot.py: collects ps/top-like output and selective /proc reads. - src/cli/samplers/trace_sampler.py: lightweight span sampler using local OTLP hooks (falls back to stack traces if OTLP not present). - templates/playbooks/latency-spike.yaml: parameterized playbook template. - templates/playbooks/oom-during-deploy.yaml: deploy-related OOM checklist. - templates/registry.json: cross-index of templates for discovery. - docs/oncall/quickdiag.md: quickstart and examples. - tests/cli/test_quickdiag_sampler.py: unit tests for sampler. - ci/workflows/quickdiag.yml: new CI job to run quickdiag tests inside a small container. Example usage: 'slo-quickdiag collect --window 30s --min-log-lines 100 --tags service=my-service --upload' will collect a 30s sampling window, attach the last 100 log lines from the service unit, annotate with tags, sign and upload the bundle and print a shareable evidence URL. Security and privacy: bundles redact known-PII patterns and enforce a size cap (8MB default). Uploads require an oncall token with minimal scope; tokens rotate via the existing secrets service. Review conversation (high level): - Ravi: "Nice cleanup — can we avoid shelling out to strace by default? Also ensure the default bundle is < 10MB." Author (Aisha): "Agreed, changed default sampler to non-strace fallback and added size heuristics; moved strace/perf to an opt-in subcommand '--expert'". - Marina: "Docs are great; add an explicit note about RBAC and token scope." Author: "Added RBAC section and linked to the secrets rotation doc." - Connor: "Test flakiness on CI: sampler tests occasionally hit a timing race on busy runners." Author: "Added deterministic mocks and retry backoff, moved to an isolated job with soft timeouts." CI summary: - unit tests: pass on first run - lint: pass - integration (containerized sampler): initially failed due to flaky timing, re-run passed - e2e upload test: pass. Merge details: squashed and merged by Marina Lopez on 2026-03-02 using 'squash and merge' with merge commit message 'oncall: quick diagnostics CLI and playbook templates catalog — squash'. Post-merge followups: - ENG-7210: integrate template registry into Console template picker (follow-up work). - ENG-7241: add incident-bot automation to suggest appropriate playbook based on initial evidence bundle (spike). - Security: schedule a short threat-model review for bundle contents (owner: Security team). Notes for oncall: This tool is intended to speed the first 5–10 minutes of triage and is not a replacement for deeper forensic tooling. Keep default behavior conservative (no kernel-level traces) and make 'expert' traces explicit. Testing notes: # of changed files reflects a small surface area but the bulk of additions are templated YAML and docs. Files changed count: 12. Metrics to watch post-ship: average time-to-first-evidence, size of uploaded bundles, frequency of expert-trace usage. If the default bundle size approaches the 8MB cap in production, we will iterate on sampling heuristics. Thank you to reviewers and SRE for quick feedback and to the docs team for polishing examples.
